claims.text:
stage computation: Two positions each accept a length2 window. Training only at position0: e1→1, e2→−1. Minimum-Euclidean-norm least squares gives tied w=[1,−1] (2parameters) and untied w0=[1,−1], w1=[0,0] (4parameters). Heldout position1 e1 with declared position-invariant target1 yields predictions1 versus0, squared errors0 versus1.

**Countercase / boundary:** Add labelled example position1 e1→−1, a position-dependent rule. Refit all three samples: tied w=[0,−1] has SSE2; untied w0=[1,−1],w1=[−1,0] has SSE0. The target invariance matters; parameter count alone does not prove real sample complexity or universal superiority.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict the unseen-position output under the tied fit; recall a new task whose labels change by position can favour untied weights.

**Intervention / reachable witness:** Fit both recomputes coefficient estimates and heldout outputs; Break invariance adds the exact third sample and refits both, retaining the initial comparison. Distinguish train SSE and heldout error explicitly.
